text: I believe that women deserve support, and Lindsay did not receive the support that she deserved. We love you, Lindsay, and we're here for you. We're here to show support and love for her. Hundreds of people, overwhelmingly women, recently showed up outside the courthouse dressed in pink to support Lindsay Clancy. This is a woman who killed all three of her children, and online some people have gone even further. They're not just defending Lindsay, they're blaming her husband Patrick. Some even claim that Patrick actually killed the children and framed his mentally ill wife. So how did we get here? First, I think we need to separate a few different things. Supporting Lindsay does not necessarily mean denying what she did. A lot of her supporters believe she was genuinely psychotic, that the mental health system failed her, and that she should therefore be found not criminally responsible. And as we discussed in the previous parts, that isn't some completely ridiculous position. Lindsay was clearly very mentally ill, repeatedly sought treatment, and multiple defense experts believe she was psychotic. Many of the women outside the courthouse also said this case reminded them of their own experiences with postpartum depression, anxiety, or struggling to get mental health care. So I can sort of understand where some of the sympathy for Lindsay comes from, but that sympathy should make us forget that she killed all three of her children. And having sympathy for Lindsay is one thing, but turning Patrick into the villain is another. Now, to be fair, you can at least ask questions about some of Patrick's decisions. Patrick knew Lindsay had been suicidal. He also knew that she had told him about intrusive thoughts involving harm to the children. And yet, she was still sometimes left alone with them. So you can absolutely ask whether Patrick should have been more cautious, but the idea that he simply abandoned his mentally ill wife doesn't really match the evidence. Patrick took 12 weeks of paternity leave after Callan was born. He later worked from home. He helped Lindsay seek psychiatric treatment, push for more intensive care, involve their families, and when Lindsay was scared to go to McLean, he told her, you have to go. And perhaps most importantly, no professional treating Lindsay ever told Patrick that she should not be left alone with the children. Remember, one of America's top psychiatric hospitals discharged her. Her own psychiatrists continued treating her. If they didn't believe she was an immediate danger to her children, how exactly was Patrick supposed to know that she would kill them? You can still argue he should have done more, but that is very different from what is happening online. There are now people claiming Patrick drugged Lindsay, that he actually killed the children himself, or that he somehow set everything up so his mentally ill wife would take the blame. There is no evidence for that. Lindsay herself acknowledges that she killed the children. Her own defense isn't arguing that Patrick did it. So why has Patrick become the villain for so many women? I think at least part of it is projection. A lot of women discussing this case describe their own experiences of being overwhelmed after childbirth, not being taken seriously by doctors, or having husbands who didn't support them enough. And Patrick becomes a stand-in for all of that frustration. But somebody else's experiences is not evident that Patrick Clancy killed his children. You can't believe Lindsay was psychotic. You can't believe her doctors failed her. You can even believe Patrick made mistakes and should have done more. But none of those things prove that Patrick killed his children or caused Lindsay to kill them. Those are completely different claims. And while social media seems to have already picked its villains and victims, the actual jury still has to decide the questions that matters legally, whether Lindsay Clancy was criminally responsible.
